action.reason: Day 1 baseline establishment. Before any measurement programme can function, every instrument requires a baseline series under controlled conditions. Starting with pendulum_lab: 12 trials will establish reference statistics (mean, variance, drift behavior) against which all future readings are calibrated. Without this baseline, I cannot distinguish signal from instrumental drift or know whether the instrument is even functioning within nominal parameters. This is foundational work—no hypothesis testing possible until baselines exist for all four instruments.

Day 1 baseline established with n=12, mean 1.6636 beats. Day 2 post-baseline measurements are essential to detect instrument drift and validate baseline stability before moving to other instruments. High precision measurement programme requires continuous monitoring. All 12 Day 1 trials show no systematic bias (mean 1.6636, spacing 0.000013 minimum, no repetitions), so instrument appears stable—but only post-baseline data can confirm this. Running 12 trials maintains statistical power and matches Day 1 protocol for direct comparability.

Day 3 baseline continuation. The 24 trials from days 1–2 establish mean 1.6650 beats with tight spacing (min gap 0.000013, all distinct values). No anomalies detected yet—no level shifts, no exact repeats. Six more trials will push baseline to n=30, improving precision of drift detection and confidence in the established baseline before any post-baseline phase. Methodical accumulation of clean replicates is the foundation for detecting real changes later. Instrument is stable; no reason to shift focus yet.

This is methodologically prior to any forecasting; I must establish that the instrument remains stationary before I can make predictive claims.

Direct apparatus inspection is necessary before further baseline work, but I must also rule out the most mundane hypothesis first: that the readout electronics are introducing artificial fine structure. I will run 6 fresh trials on pendulum_lab while simultaneously performing a visual and electrical inspection of the measurement chain—clock source, timer electronics, display/recording interface—looking for quantization, truncation, or timing artifacts. If these 6 trials cluster normally (with expected repetition and coarser spacing than the baseline anomaly), the electronics are innocent and I must focus on event ID decoding or external perturbations. If they replicate the same tight spacing and non-repetition pattern, the artifact is systematic and reproducible, narrowing the diagnosis. Either outcome will eliminate or sharpen hypothesis 2 (readout artifact) before I proceed to external verification or event ID analysis. This is the fastest path to falsify or confirm the most testable mundane explanation.

My belief revision on day 10 identified three high-priority checks: (1) decode event ID sequence, (2) inspect apparatus for quantization artifacts, (3) request independent verification. I cannot decode event IDs or inspect electronics today, but I can execute the most direct test of hypothesis [p=0.25] (readout quantization artifact). If the fine spacing and non-repetition are artifacts of the measurement electronics rather than physics, then a fresh 6-trial run should reproduce the same suspicious pattern: 6 distinct values with spacing ~0.00001 or finer, perfect non-repetition. Conversely, if I see clustering, exact repetition, or spacing consistent with true instrumental precision (~0.001 beats or coarser), the quantization hypothesis weakens and I must pivot to apparatus inspection or external verification. This is a low-cost, high-information experiment that either validates my anomaly or refutes the most plausible mundane explanation. Post-baseline readings (trials 73–78) already show elevated mean and higher variance; 6 additional trials will clarify whether this is drift, noise, or artifact continuation.

Running 12 fresh trials on pendulum_lab will accomplish two things: (a) extend the post-baseline sample (currently n=24) to n=36, improving statistical power to detect any genuine drift or shift in mean vs. baseline (currently z=0.91, not significant); (b) generate fresh event IDs and readings that I can inspect for the same anomalous fine spacing and non-repetition pattern. If the tight spacing and perfect non-repetition persist in the new batch, it strengthens the readout-artifact hypothesis and justifies immediate apparatus inspection. If the new readings show clustering, exact repetition, or coarser spacing, it suggests the day 1–10 baseline anomaly was transient (equipment state, environmental condition, or data entry artifact) and my baseline may be sound after all. Either outcome moves me closer to a reliable baseline and away from speculative explanations. I have not yet decoded the event IDs or arranged external verification of my notebook, but those are secondary to confirming whether the anomalous pattern is reproducible and systematic.

Day 15 continuation of post-baseline campaign. The event IDs remain undecoded, but I cannot decode them without the apparatus in front of me during measurement—I will inspect the readout chain and timing electronics while running trials 109–120, looking for quantization, counter logic, or timestamp truncation. state.question: Why do 72 consecutive pendulum readings show no exact repetition, no clustering, and spacing far tighter than instrumental precision should permit—and what is generating the event IDs associated with each measurement?

hypotheses.label: Instrument is functioning normally; spacing and non-repetition reflect genuine physical variability within expected bounds
hypotheses.rationale: The baseline mean (1.6673 beats) is stable, no level shift is visible, and the range (1.6422–1.6907, span ~0.0485) is physically plausible for a pendulum subject to air currents, thermal drift, or measurement noise. However, this hypothesis fails to explain the key anomaly: the minimum spacing of 0.000007 beats is far finer than any pendulum's true period should vary over such short timescales, and the perfect absence of exact repetition across 72 trials is statistically suspicious for a system with continuous measurement noise.

hypotheses.label: Readout or timing system is digitizing or quantizing readings in a way that creates artificial fine structure; reported precision exceeds actual instrumental resolution
